name: Tribunal of Brescia, judgment no. 843/2026 of 17 March 2026 (Rep. no. 3553/2026) – air quality PM10/NO2
date: 17 March 2026 (filed) (signed on 16 March 2026); chronological judgment no. 843/2026, Rep. no. 3553/2026, R.G. no. 11098/2024

jurisdiction.court: Tribunal of Brescia, First Civil Section (single judge)

description: More than seventy citizens residing (or who have resided) in municipalities of Lombardy brought proceedings against the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, the Ministry of the Environment and Energy Security and the Lombardy Region (with the third-party joinder of Generali Italia s.p.a. and Unipol Assicurazioni s.p.a.) before the Civil Tribunal of Brescia, seeking: (i) an order requiring the administrations to adopt the measures provided for by national and Community legislation on air quality, including information obligations and plans for compliance with the limit values; (ii) a penalty payment for each day of delay in compliance; (iii) compensation for non-pecuniary damage under Articles 2043 and 2059 of the Italian Civil Code for the violation of the relevant rights. The claimants based their claims on the judgments of the Court of Justice of the European Union of 10 November 2020 (Case C-644/18, exceedance of the PM10 limits from 2008 to 2017) and of 12 May 2022 (Case C-573/19, exceedance of the NO2 limits from 2010 to 2018), as well as on the Francovich case law on State liability for infringement of EU law.
outcome: The Tribunal declared the claim inadmissible for absolute lack of jurisdiction. As regards the request for an order to act (ordine di facere) addressed to the administrations, the judge held that the adoption of air quality plans and measures falls within political choices reserved to the governing bodies, which the ordinary judicial authority cannot review by virtue of the principle of separation of powers. As regards the claim for damages, the Tribunal referred to the judgment of the CJEU of 22 December 2022 (Case C-61/21, Responsabilité de l'État pour la pollution de l'air) to exclude that Directive 2008/50/EC confers on individuals rights whose infringement may give rise to the State's liability in damages, characterising the interest in air quality as a diffuse interest that cannot be independently protected in court by an individual citizen (also referring to Italian Council of State, Plenary Session, no. 6/2020). The claimants were ordered to pay the costs in favour of each defendant administration (EUR 5,333.00 in fees, plus ancillary charges); costs were set off as between the claimants and the insurance companies joined in the proceedings.
